findings.evidenceJa: 誰かと手合わせする
findings.governingReading: Shirou has not sparred with another person in years.
findings.explanation: A practice bout becomes a competitive contest, changing why he cleans the dojo as a courtesy.

findings.highlight: I wonder what she’ll make me do
findings.evidenceJa: 剣の修行って言っても
findings.governingReading: Shirou specifically wonders what sword training will involve.
findings.explanation: The English drops the governing activity and leaves a generic apprehension.

findings.highlight: It seems Saber has come up with a solution on her own too.
findings.evidenceJa: ただの思い違いだからいいんだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou immediately corrects Saber’s mistaken offer to change into armor.
findings.explanation: The English inserts a narration line claiming Saber found a solution when she has actually misunderstood him.

findings.evidenceJa: 無茶でもなんでも言ってくれ
findings.governingReading: Shirou hands Saber control of the regimen and invites even unreasonable demands.
findings.explanation: The English loses the extremity of his permission and produces an unclear “give me anything.”

findings.evidenceJa: まじまじとこちらを見つめていた
findings.governingReading: Distracted Saber receives the shinai and stares intently at Shirou.
findings.explanation: The generic look removes the prolonged scrutiny marking her reaction to his clothing remarks.

findings.evidenceJa: 良かった
findings.governingReading: Shirou simply expresses relief that Saber will not require wooden or live blades.
findings.explanation: The English adds a religious invocation to his casual relief.

findings.highlight: your strength is up to standards
findings.evidenceJa: 運動能力は水準に達しています
findings.governingReading: Saber judges Shirou’s overall athletic ability to have reached the required level.
findings.explanation: The English narrows coordination, speed, endurance, and strength to strength alone.

findings.evidenceJa: それが幸いしたのでしょう
findings.governingReading: Saber says Shirou’s long physical training paid off when Lancer attacked.
findings.explanation: A causal payoff from effort becomes luck, contradicting her next sentence crediting that effort.

findings.evidenceJa: 世界が暗転した
findings.governingReading: Saber’s opening hit makes Shirou’s world go black as he loses consciousness.
findings.explanation: The English changes blackout into spatial inversion.

findings.highlight: It is indeed only a bruise
findings.evidenceJa: 確かに打ち身ではありますが
findings.governingReading: Saber confirms the injury is a bruise but warns that it must not be moved immediately.
findings.explanation: The added “only” minimizes the severe contusion she identified on the preceding page.

findings.evidenceJa: 疲労困憊して足場も不確か
findings.governingReading: Saber rejects training while Shirou is exhausted and his footing is unreliable on the sweaty floor.
findings.explanation: The English removes the unstable footing, one of the concrete conditions behind her tactical rule.

findings.evidenceJa: 的確な状況を模索する
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s battle begins by seeking an apt, precisely favorable situation.
findings.explanation: The English upgrades tactical suitability into perfection, overstating what Saber requires.

findings.highlight: my body is burning with pain
findings.evidenceJa: 体中がズキズキと痛む
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s whole body aches and throbs after the blows.
findings.explanation: The English changes the pain quality to burning, importing the heat image from his preceding breath.

findings.evidenceJa: 軽い失神
findings.governingReading: Saber’s first strikes cause brief or light loss of consciousness.
findings.explanation: “Faint slightly” treats a binary event as a degree and produces unnatural English.

findings.evidenceJa: 戦力差
findings.governingReading: Shirou confronts the total gap in fighting power between himself and Saber.
findings.explanation: The English narrows the disparity to learned skill alone.

findings.evidenceJa: 直感がビシバシ来る
findings.governingReading: Danger intuitions strike Shirou sharply and repeatedly whenever a blow would knock him out.
findings.explanation: The English renders intensity and repetition as countable instincts, obscuring the learned warning response.

findings.evidenceJa: 竹刀をなんとか受け流して
findings.governingReading: Shirou barely parries or redirects Saber’s rain of shinai strikes.
findings.explanation: The English changes active weapon defense into evasive movement.

findings.highlight: She’s admiring needless things with gentle eyes.
findings.evidenceJa: 熱心さに対応を忘れたほどです
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese ends with Saber saying Shirou’s earnestness sometimes made her forget to respond.
findings.explanation: The English restores a commented-out sentence assigning gentle eyes and dismissing her praise as needless.

findings.evidenceJa: 行儀良く道場に正座している
findings.governingReading: Saber waits properly in seiza on the dojo floor.
findings.explanation: The English omits the concrete posture and leaves an ungrammatical style phrase.

findings.highlight: I feel she is beautiful in everyone’s eyes
findings.evidenceJa: 人間として綺麗と思う
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he finds Saber beautiful as one human being regarding another, rather than specifically as a man viewing a woman.
findings.explanation: The English turns his chosen mode of regard into a claim about everyone’s opinion.

findings.highlight: She has melted into the dignified atmosphere of the dojo, and has a quietness free of any conflicts.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーのサーヴァントであり、戦いを肯とする事
findings.governingReading: The active page begins with Shirou’s discomfort that this beautiful person is a Saber-class Servant who affirms battle.
findings.explanation: The English restores a commented-out idealized description of her merging with the dojo’s tranquil atmosphere.
